brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Three columns: a centre stack of three full bases (0,0, levels 0–2) with a half-s base stack two levels high on each side, (-1,0) and (1,0). Top covers on all three columns make the shelf surfaces. A row of books (prop) stands on the top cover. The west column is joined to the centre with joint bolts at levels 0 and 1.
drawer:0#-1,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut, each fitted on the cut face of a level-0 half base.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator only checks fit and collisions. It has no load ratings, and strength depends on the print material and settings, so I can't show a 50 kg rating.

finish.summary: I built a three-column shelf unit with two drawers at the bottom. check_build found no rule errors and the parts don't collide. The 50 kg rating is unmet: the configurator can't check load capacity.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
